What it is

Nets are great. Living with them isn't.

LiftNets is a motorized lifting system that raises an entire net enclosure into the ceiling of your structure — and lowers it back down on demand. When the net is up, you get your space back: open pavilion, party lawn, parking, whatever you want. When it's down, you have a full professional-grade cage.

1 buttonto raise or lower the full enclosure
Any sizecustom-built systems from 24' to 72'+
Any netsports mesh, mosquito netting, steel mesh
How it works

Two rings, one winch, zero hassle.

The system installs into new or existing structures — pavilions, gazebos, barns, court canopies — and runs off a simple 12-volt drive.

01

Upper ring

A rigid ring mounts overhead in your structure. It carries the upper net, the routing pulleys, and the lifting cables.

02

Lower ring + net

The net hangs from a matching lower ring. Lowered, it seals the enclosure top to bottom. Raised, the whole net gathers neatly at the ceiling.

03

Drive motor

An industrial 12V hoist with a weatherproof control box does the lifting. Press up. Press down. That's the entire user manual.

The story

Built for a grandson. Engineered for everyone.

It started with a simple problem: a grandson who loves baseball, and a beautiful backyard that a permanent batting cage would ruin. Inspired by touchless boat covers, Craig Hanson — a career engineer — designed a lifting system that raises the entire net into the pavilion roof when it's not in use.

The first system is built, tested, and gets swung in daily. Every part is fabricated and pre-assembled in our own shop.
